summary: The LLM landscape in late 2026 is dominated by frontier models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google, with adoption increasingly driven by enterprise consumption through cloud aggregators like AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, Google Vertex AI, and Snowflake Cortex. Open-weight models from DeepSeek, Meta, Mistral, and Alibaba have captured significant developer mindshare due to dramatic cost reductions and strong performance. Because much of the live research data references unverifiable or speculative version numbers, this ranking conservatively uses only model names that can be confirmed as publicly released and currently available.

models.name: GPT-4o
models.popularity_notes: Consistently the highest-volume model by API calls and developer survey mentions, and broadly available through Azure OpenAI and other enterprise aggregators, giving it massive real-world reach.
models.best_for: General-purpose multimodal applications and production chat assistants

models.name: Claude Sonnet 4.6
models.popularity_notes: Confirmed in research as shipped February 17 matching Opus-level performance at Sonnet pricing, and widely consumed through AWS Bedrock and Google Vertex AI, boosting enterprise adoption significantly.
models.best_for: Software development and agentic coding workflows

models.name: Gemini 2.5 Pro
models.popularity_notes: Known as the context-window king in coding comparisons and natively distributed via Google Vertex AI, driving strong enterprise and developer adoption.
models.best_for: Large-context document analysis and multimodal reasoning tasks

models.name: DeepSeek R1
models.popularity_notes: A 671B MoE reasoning model cited as the cheapest frontier-class model at $0.55/$2.19 per 1M tokens, with heavy HuggingFace downloads and growing aggregator availability.
models.best_for: Cost-sensitive reasoning and mathematical problem solving

models.name: DeepSeek V3
models.popularity_notes: The general-purpose counterpart to R1 with very strong price-performance, widely downloaded on HuggingFace and increasingly offered through third-party inference providers.

models.name: Gemini 2.5 Flash
models.popularity_notes: The low-latency, low-cost variant with a large context window referenced in research, heavily used in high-throughput production via Vertex AI.

models.name: Claude Haiku 4.5
models.popularity_notes: Anthropic's fast, affordable tier widely adopted for scaled applications and available through AWS Bedrock and Google Vertex AI for enterprise consumption.
models.best_for: Fast, cost-efficient assistant and classification tasks

models.name: Llama 3.3 70B
models.popularity_notes: One of the most downloaded open-weight models on HuggingFace and offered across AWS Bedrock, Azure, and Google Vertex AI, giving it enormous real-world deployment footprint.
strengths: Strong general performance for its size

models.name: Qwen3-235B-A22B
models.popularity_notes: A leading open-weight MoE model with strong benchmark results and rapidly growing HuggingFace downloads, especially popular in Asian markets and self-hosting communities.

models.name: Mistral Large 2
models.popularity_notes: Europe's leading frontier model, favored for data-sovereignty-conscious deployments and available through Azure AI and AWS Bedrock, strengthening its enterprise reach.
models.best_for: European enterprise deployments with data-sovereignty needs

models.name: o3
models.popularity_notes: OpenAI's dedicated reasoning model with strong adoption for complex analytical and coding tasks, available through Azure OpenAI, clustering closely with the top-10 enterprise reasoning options.
models.best_for: Complex reasoning, math, and advanced coding tasks
